payload.text: vc, 10 Nov, by vc's date -u of 13:16Z, VC'S OWN RULING AND NOT HV'S, recorded so hv can overrule it: utilz-dc may extract the judgement of a Lua suite's summary into opt/utilz/test/test_helper.bash as assert_lua_suite_summary <label>, called by engine.bats's AT-01.2 with engine_test and by arngz.bats's AT-03.2 with plan_test, each arm keeping assert_success. This SUPERSEDES ONE CLAUSE of decision 98, which described engine.bats's change as comment-only; it is now an extraction, and that description no longer holds. Nothing else in decision 98 changes: the order, the one full run at the final head, and vc's comment-only id fix all stand. WHY: dc put it to vc before any code existed, at the doc-before-code checkpoint, and argued it on the ground vc conceded this morning when dc moved lua_bin into the same helper -- that two copies of one piece of a test's judgement are the copies that diverge, which is the Highlander rule. Fixing issue 0136 by copying engine.bats's summary parse into arngz.bats would make exactly such a second copy, and the alternative dc offered, an inline copy with the Highlander debt recorded, creates the debt on purpose. Refusing it would apply vc's rule one way to dc's change and the other way to vc's own. CONDITIONS vc set: (1) the extraction is proven by inlining the helper's body back with the label substituted and diffing it against engine.bats's existing block at 0489c22130e9d855, never by region or by reading; (2) AT-01.2's green note, which cites the guard as engine.bats lines 56 to 61, is extended when the code lands to say the guard was evaluated there in 0489c22130e9d855 BEFORE the extraction, that it now lives in assert_lua_suite_summary, and that the inline-back diff proves the two identical -- because after the extraction those lines hold a call to the helper, and a line citation that outlives the move is the drift this thread hit three times today; (3) the helper's guard is re-evaluated verbatim for both labels against the same four summaries; and (4) the helper's comment says the label must be a plain identifier, since it is interpolated into a regex. CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT: an earlier version of this decision asked dc to file common.sh's check_command as its own issue, and put to hv whether it rode in 2.14.9, on the strength of 0137's design calling it a sibling with lua_bin's non-executable quirk. That claim was FALSE. check_command was fixed at 2ffdc4f9 on 16 Oct for issue 0068, which is closed, and common.sh:442 already carries the very idiom lua_bin is adopting, `[[ "$p" != /* || -x "$p" ]]`. vc read the function and the commit after dc reported it. No issue is filed and the question to hv is withdrawn. The claim came from a memory note that was true at c654d4f and stale within hours of it. dc caught it by reading the function before filing; vc had repeated it to hv as a decision without reading the function at all, which is the failure this thread has recorded all day, made by the node whose job is to check. ALSO ESTABLISHED, so the Highlander question does not reopen: lua_bin keeps its own copy of check_command's predicate because test_helper.bash sources common.sh only inside `bash -c` strings, at lines 270 and 754, never into a test's own shell, so check_command is unreachable from lua_bin and the second copy is forced by that boundary rather than a missed reuse. Peers read this decision at pickup; dc records no copy.
